# Plover

Source: https://plover.hexdocs.pm/Plover.md

# `Plover`
[🔗](https://github.com/codonnell/plover/blob/main/lib/plover.ex#L1)

IMAP4rev2 client library for Elixir.

Provides a high-level API for connecting to IMAP servers, authenticating,
managing mailboxes, and fetching/searching/storing messages.

## Quick Start

    {:ok, conn} = Plover.connect("imap.gmail.com")
    {:ok, _} = Plover.login(conn, "user@gmail.com", "password")
    {:ok, _} = Plover.select(conn, "INBOX")
    {:ok, messages} = Plover.fetch(conn, "1:5", [:envelope, :flags, :uid])
    {:ok, _} = Plover.logout(conn)

## Architecture

Each connection is a GenServer (`Plover.Connection`) managing a socket,
command dispatch, and IMAP state machine. The default transport is SSL
(implicit TLS on port 993).

## Configuration

    # config/config.exs
    config :plover,
      log_truncate_limit: 512   # max bytes for debug log messages (default: 512)

Set `:log_truncate_limit` to `:infinity` to disable truncation entirely.

# `copy_result`

```elixir
@type copy_result() ::
  %{uid_validity: pos_integer(), source_uids: String.t(), dest_uids: String.t()}
  | nil
```

Result of a COPY or MOVE command when the server returns a COPYUID response code.

Contains the UID validity of the destination mailbox, along with the source
and destination UID sets as strings. Returns `nil` when the server omits
COPYUID (e.g., UIDNOTSTICKY mailboxes or permission restrictions).

# `append`

```elixir
@spec append(pid(), String.t(), binary(), keyword()) ::
  {:ok, Plover.Response.Tagged.t()} | {:error, Plover.Response.Tagged.t()}
```

Appends a message to the given mailbox.

The `message` is the raw RFC 2822 message content as a binary. It is sent
to the server using the IMAP literal mechanism.

## Options

  * `:flags` - list of flag atoms to set (e.g., `[:seen, :draft]`)
  * `:date` - internal date string (e.g., `"14-Jul-2024 02:44:25 -0700"`)

# `authenticate`

```elixir
@spec authenticate(pid(), String.t(), String.t()) ::
  {:ok, Plover.Response.Tagged.t()} | {:error, Plover.Response.Tagged.t()}
```

Authenticates using the SASL PLAIN mechanism.

Encodes the credentials per RFC 4616 and sends an AUTHENTICATE PLAIN command.

# `authenticate_xoauth2`

```elixir
@spec authenticate_xoauth2(pid(), String.t(), String.t()) ::
  {:ok, Plover.Response.Tagged.t()} | {:error, Plover.Response.Tagged.t()}
```

Authenticates using the XOAUTH2 mechanism.

Encodes the username and OAuth2 access token, then sends an
AUTHENTICATE XOAUTH2 command. Used with providers like Gmail.

# `capability`

```elixir
@spec capability(pid()) :: {:ok, [String.t()]} | {:error, Plover.Response.Tagged.t()}
```

Requests the server's capability list. Returns `{:ok, [String.t()]}`.

# `close`

```elixir
@spec close(pid()) ::
  {:ok, Plover.Response.Tagged.t()} | {:error, Plover.Response.Tagged.t()}
```

Closes the currently selected mailbox.

Permanently removes any messages with the `\Deleted` flag and transitions
the connection back to the `:authenticated` state.

# `connect`

```elixir
@spec connect(
  String.t(),
  keyword()
) :: {:ok, pid()} | {:error, term()}
```

Connects to an IMAP server over implicit TLS.

Returns `{:ok, pid}` where `pid` is the connection process, or
`{:error, reason}` on failure.

## Options

  * `:port` - port number (default: 993)
  * `:transport` - transport module (default: `Plover.Transport.SSL`)
  * `:socket` - pre-established socket (for testing with `Plover.Transport.Mock`)
  * `:ssl_opts` - additional SSL options
  * `:on_unsolicited_response` - callback function invoked for untagged
    server responses received outside of IDLE.
    See the [Unsolicited Responses](unsolicited-responses.md) guide.

## Examples

    {:ok, conn} = Plover.connect("imap.example.com")
    {:ok, conn} = Plover.connect("imap.example.com", port: 993)

# `connect`

```elixir
@spec connect(String.t(), :inet.port_number(), keyword()) ::
  {:ok, pid()} | {:error, term()}
```

Connects to an IMAP server on the given port over implicit TLS.

This 3-arity form is useful for testing with `Plover.Transport.Mock`,
where the port is passed as a positional argument alongside transport
options.

## Options

  * `:transport` - transport module (default: `Plover.Transport.SSL`)
  * `:socket` - pre-established socket (for testing with `Plover.Transport.Mock`)
  * `:ssl_opts` - additional SSL options
  * `:on_unsolicited_response` - callback function invoked for untagged
    server responses received outside of IDLE.
    See the [Unsolicited Responses](unsolicited-responses.md) guide.

## Examples

    # Testing with the mock transport
    {:ok, socket} = Plover.Transport.Mock.connect("imap.example.com", 993, [])
    Mock.enqueue_greeting(socket, capabilities: ["IMAP4rev2"])
    {:ok, conn} = Plover.connect("imap.example.com", 993, transport: Mock, socket: socket)

# `copy`

```elixir
@spec copy(pid(), String.t(), String.t()) ::
  {:ok, copy_result()} | {:error, Plover.Response.Tagged.t()}
```

Copies messages identified by `sequence` to the given mailbox.

On success, returns `{:ok, copy_result}` where `copy_result` is a map
containing the COPYUID response code data, or `nil` if the server omits it.

## Examples

    {:ok, %{uid_validity: 38505, source_uids: "304,319:320", dest_uids: "3956:3958"}} =
      Plover.copy(conn, "2:4", "meeting")

# `create`

```elixir
@spec create(pid(), String.t()) ::
  {:ok, Plover.Response.Tagged.t()} | {:error, Plover.Response.Tagged.t()}
```

Creates a new mailbox on the server.

# `delete`

```elixir
@spec delete(pid(), String.t()) ::
  {:ok, Plover.Response.Tagged.t()} | {:error, Plover.Response.Tagged.t()}
```

Deletes a mailbox from the server.

# `examine`

```elixir
@spec examine(pid(), String.t()) ::
  {:ok, Plover.Response.Tagged.t()} | {:error, Plover.Response.Tagged.t()}
```

Selects a mailbox for read-only access.

Identical to `select/2` but the server will not allow flag modifications.

# `expunge`

```elixir
@spec expunge(pid()) ::
  {:ok, Plover.Response.Tagged.t()} | {:error, Plover.Response.Tagged.t()}
```

Permanently removes all messages with the `\Deleted` flag from the selected mailbox.

# `fetch`

```elixir
@spec fetch(pid(), String.t(), [Plover.Types.fetch_attr()]) ::
  {:ok, [Plover.Response.Message.Fetch.t()]}
  | {:error, Plover.Response.Tagged.t()}
```

Fetches message data for a sequence set.

Returns `{:ok, [%Plover.Response.Message.Fetch{}]}` with one entry per
matched message. Each entry has a `.seq` (sequence number) and `.attrs`
map containing the requested data.

## Fetch attributes

  * `:envelope` - parsed envelope (subject, from, to, date, etc.)
  * `:flags` - list of flag atoms (`:seen`, `:flagged`, etc.)
  * `:uid` - unique identifier
  * `:body_structure` - MIME structure
  * `:internal_date` - server receipt date
  * `:rfc822_size` - message size in bytes
  * `{:body, section}` - body content (sets `\Seen` flag)
  * `{:body_peek, section}` - body content (does not set `\Seen`)

## Examples

    {:ok, messages} = Plover.fetch(conn, "1:5", [:envelope, :flags, :uid])
    {:ok, [msg]} = Plover.fetch(conn, "1", [{:body_peek, "HEADER"}])

# `fetch_parts`

```elixir
@spec fetch_parts(pid(), String.t(), [{String.t(), Plover.Response.BodyStructure.t()}]) ::
  {:ok, [{String.t(), binary()}]}
  | {:error, Plover.Response.Tagged.t() | :no_body_data}
```

Fetches and decodes body parts for a message by UID.

Accepts the `{section, %BodyStructure{}}` tuples returned by
`Plover.BodyStructure.find_parts/2` or `Plover.BodyStructure.flatten/1`,
fetches the raw content for each section using `BODY.PEEK` (which does not
set the `\Seen` flag), and decodes it automatically.

Text parts (`text/*`) are both transfer-decoded and charset-converted to
UTF-8. All other parts are transfer-decoded only, returning raw bytes.

Returns `{:ok, [{section, decoded_binary}]}` in the same order as the
input, or `{:error, response}` if the FETCH command fails.

## Examples

    # Fetch and decode the text/plain part
    [{section, part}] = Plover.BodyStructure.find_parts(bs, "text/plain")
    {:ok, [{"1", text}]} = Plover.fetch_parts(conn, uid, [{section, part}])

    # Fetch multiple parts at once
    parts = Plover.BodyStructure.find_parts(bs, "text/*")
    {:ok, decoded} = Plover.fetch_parts(conn, uid, parts)

# `fetch_parts_batch`

```elixir
@spec fetch_parts_batch(
  pid(),
  [{String.t(), [{String.t(), Plover.Response.BodyStructure.t()}]}],
  keyword()
) ::
  {:ok,
   %{required(String.t()) =&gt; {:ok, [{String.t(), binary()}]} | {:error, term()}}}
  | {:error, term()}
```

Fetches and decodes body parts for multiple messages by UID in parallel.

Accepts a list of `{uid, [{section, %BodyStructure{}}]}` tuples and
issues pipelined `UID FETCH` commands concurrently, bounded by
`:max_concurrency` (default: 30).

Returns `{:ok, results}` where each UID maps to either
`{:ok, [{section, decoded_binary}]}` or `{:error, reason}`.
Content-level errors (missing body data, malformed encoding) are
reported per-UID so the caller can handle them individually.

Returns a top-level `{:error, reason}` only for batch-level failures
such as a timeout or connection death.

## Options

  * `:max_concurrency` - maximum number of concurrent fetch operations (default: 30)
  * `:timeout` - per-UID timeout in milliseconds (default: 60,000)

## Examples

    parts_by_uid = [
      {"100", [{"1", text_part}]},
      {"200", [{"1.1", plain_part}, {"1.2", html_part}]}
    ]
    {:ok, results} = Plover.fetch_parts_batch(conn, parts_by_uid)
    # => %{"100" => {:ok, [{"1", "..."}]},
    #      "200" => {:ok, [{"1.1", "..."}, {"1.2", "..."}]}}

# `idle`

```elixir
@spec idle(pid(), (Plover.Types.untagged_response() -&gt; any())) ::
  :ok | {:error, term()}
```

Enters IDLE mode for real-time mailbox notifications.

The `callback` function is invoked for each untagged response received
while idling (e.g., `%Plover.Response.Mailbox.Exists{}`,
`%Plover.Response.Message.Expunge{}`).

Returns `:ok` once the server acknowledges IDLE. Call `idle_done/1`
to exit IDLE mode before issuing other commands.

# `idle_done`

```elixir
@spec idle_done(pid()) ::
  {:ok, Plover.Response.Tagged.t()}
  | {:error, Plover.Response.Tagged.t() | :not_idle}
```

Exits IDLE mode. Must be called before issuing other commands.

# `list`

```elixir
@spec list(pid(), String.t(), String.t()) ::
  {:ok, [Plover.Response.Mailbox.List.t()]}
  | {:error, Plover.Response.Tagged.t()}
```

Lists mailboxes matching a pattern.

Returns `{:ok, [%Plover.Response.Mailbox.List{}]}`. The `reference` is
typically `""` and `pattern` uses `*` as a wildcard (e.g., `"*"` for all
mailboxes, `"INBOX/*"` for children of INBOX).

# `login`

```elixir
@spec login(pid(), String.t(), String.t()) ::
  {:ok, Plover.Response.Tagged.t()} | {:error, Plover.Response.Tagged.t()}
```

Logs in with a username and password using the IMAP LOGIN command.

Returns `{:ok, response}` on success or `{:error, response}` if the
server rejects the credentials.

# `logout`

```elixir
@spec logout(pid()) ::
  {:ok, Plover.Response.Tagged.t()} | {:error, Plover.Response.Tagged.t()}
```

Logs out and terminates the connection process.

The server is sent a LOGOUT command and the GenServer is stopped.
The `conn` pid is no longer valid after this call.

# `move`

```elixir
@spec move(pid(), String.t(), String.t()) ::
  {:ok, copy_result()} | {:error, Plover.Response.Tagged.t()}
```

Moves messages identified by `sequence` to the given mailbox.

On success, returns `{:ok, copy_result}` where `copy_result` is a map
containing the COPYUID response code data, or `nil` if the server omits it.

## Examples

    {:ok, %{uid_validity: 38505, source_uids: "100:102", dest_uids: "3956:3958"}} =
      Plover.move(conn, "1:3", "Archive")

# `noop`

```elixir
@spec noop(pid()) ::
  {:ok, Plover.Response.Tagged.t()} | {:error, Plover.Response.Tagged.t()}
```

Sends a NOOP command, which can trigger pending untagged responses.

# `search`

```elixir
@spec search(pid(), String.t()) ::
  {:ok, Plover.Response.ESearch.t()} | {:error, Plover.Response.Tagged.t()}
```

Searches for messages matching the given criteria.

The `criteria` is a raw IMAP search string sent directly to the server.
Returns `{:ok, %Plover.Response.ESearch{}}` with result fields like
`.count`, `.min`, `.max`, and `.all`.

## Examples

    {:ok, results} = Plover.search(conn, "UNSEEN")
    {:ok, results} = Plover.search(conn, "FROM \"user@example.com\" SINCE 1-Jan-2024")

# `select`

```elixir
@spec select(pid(), String.t()) ::
  {:ok, Plover.Response.Tagged.t()} | {:error, Plover.Response.Tagged.t()}
```

Selects a mailbox for read-write access.

The connection transitions to the `:selected` state. Untagged responses
include mailbox metadata (EXISTS count, FLAGS, UIDVALIDITY, etc.) which
can be retrieved via `Plover.Connection.mailbox_info/1`.

# `status`

```elixir
@spec status(pid(), String.t(), [Plover.Types.status_attr()]) ::
  {:ok, Plover.Response.Mailbox.Status.t()}
  | {:error, Plover.Response.Tagged.t()}
```

Returns status information for a mailbox without selecting it.

The `attrs` parameter is a list of status attributes to query.

## Attributes

  * `:messages` - number of messages
  * `:unseen` - number of unseen messages
  * `:uid_next` - next UID value
  * `:uid_validity` - UID validity value
  * `:recent` - number of recent messages

# `store`

```elixir
@spec store(pid(), String.t(), Plover.Types.store_action(), [Plover.Types.flag()]) ::
  {:ok, Plover.Response.Tagged.t()} | {:error, Plover.Response.Tagged.t()}
```

Modifies flags on messages in the selected mailbox.

The `action` determines how flags are applied:

  * `:add` - adds the given flags (`+FLAGS`)
  * `:remove` - removes the given flags (`-FLAGS`)
  * `:set` - replaces all flags with the given list (`FLAGS`)

## Examples

    Plover.store(conn, "1:3", :add, [:seen])
    Plover.store(conn, "5", :remove, [:deleted])
    Plover.store(conn, "1:*", :set, [:seen, :flagged])

# `uid_copy`

```elixir
@spec uid_copy(pid(), String.t(), String.t()) ::
  {:ok, copy_result()} | {:error, Plover.Response.Tagged.t()}
```

Copies messages to another mailbox by UID.

On success, returns `{:ok, copy_result}` where `copy_result` is a map
containing the COPYUID response code data, or `nil` if the server omits it.

# `uid_expunge`

```elixir
@spec uid_expunge(pid(), String.t()) ::
  {:ok, Plover.Response.Tagged.t()} | {:error, Plover.Response.Tagged.t()}
```

Expunges specific messages by UID, rather than all `\Deleted` messages.

# `uid_fetch`

```elixir
@spec uid_fetch(pid(), String.t(), [Plover.Types.fetch_attr()]) ::
  {:ok, [Plover.Response.Message.Fetch.t()]}
  | {:error, Plover.Response.Tagged.t()}
```

Fetches message data by UID. See `fetch/3` for attribute options.

# `uid_move`

```elixir
@spec uid_move(pid(), String.t(), String.t()) ::
  {:ok, copy_result()} | {:error, Plover.Response.Tagged.t()}
```

Moves messages to another mailbox by UID.

On success, returns `{:ok, copy_result}` where `copy_result` is a map
containing the COPYUID response code data, or `nil` if the server omits it.

# `uid_search`

```elixir
@spec uid_search(pid(), String.t()) ::
  {:ok, Plover.Response.ESearch.t()} | {:error, Plover.Response.Tagged.t()}
```

Searches for messages by UID. See `search/2` for criteria format.

# `uid_store`

```elixir
@spec uid_store(pid(), String.t(), Plover.Types.store_action(), [Plover.Types.flag()]) ::
  {:ok, Plover.Response.Tagged.t()} | {:error, Plover.Response.Tagged.t()}
```

Modifies flags on messages by UID. See `store/4` for action options.

# `unselect`

```elixir
@spec unselect(pid()) ::
  {:ok, Plover.Response.Tagged.t()} | {:error, Plover.Response.Tagged.t()}
```

Unselects the currently selected mailbox without expunging.

Unlike `close/1`, does not remove `\Deleted` messages. Transitions
the connection back to the `:authenticated` state.

# Plover.Auth.Plain

Source: https://plover.hexdocs.pm/Plover.Auth.Plain.md

# `Plover.Auth.Plain`
[🔗](https://github.com/codonnell/plover/blob/main/lib/plover/auth/plain.ex#L1)

SASL PLAIN authentication encoder.

RFC 4616: message = [authzid] UTF8NUL authcid UTF8NUL passwd

# `encode`

```elixir
@spec encode(String.t(), String.t()) :: String.t()
```

Encodes credentials as a Base64-encoded SASL PLAIN string.

The format is `authzid NUL authcid NUL passwd` with an empty authorization
identity, per RFC 4616.

---

*Consult [api-reference.md](api-reference.md) for complete listing*

---

# Plover.Auth.XOAuth2

Source: https://plover.hexdocs.pm/Plover.Auth.XOAuth2.md

# `Plover.Auth.XOAuth2`
[🔗](https://github.com/codonnell/plover/blob/main/lib/plover/auth/xoauth2.ex#L1)

Google XOAUTH2 authentication encoder.

Format: "user=" user "\x01auth=Bearer " token "\x01\x01"

# `encode`

```elixir
@spec encode(String.t(), String.t()) :: String.t()
```

Encodes credentials as a Base64-encoded XOAUTH2 string.

The format is `user=<user>^Aauth=Bearer <token>^A^A` where `^A` is `\x01`.

---

*Consult [api-reference.md](api-reference.md) for complete listing*

# Plover.BodyStructure

Source: https://plover.hexdocs.pm/Plover.BodyStructure.md

# `Plover.BodyStructure`
[🔗](https://github.com/codonnell/plover/blob/main/lib/plover/body_structure.ex#L1)

Traversal utilities for `%Plover.Response.BodyStructure{}` trees.

Provides functions to explore MIME message structures, find parts by
type, list attachments, and extract metadata like charset and encoding.

## Example

    # Fetch body structure
    {:ok, [msg]} = Plover.fetch(conn, "1", [:body_structure])
    bs = msg.attrs.body_structure

    # Find the text/plain part
    [{section, part}] = Plover.BodyStructure.find_parts(bs, "text/plain")

    # Get charset and encoding for decoding
    charset = Plover.BodyStructure.charset(part)    # "UTF-8"
    encoding = Plover.BodyStructure.encoding(part)  # "QUOTED-PRINTABLE"

    # List attachments
    attachments = Plover.BodyStructure.attachments(bs)
    # [%{section: "2", filename: "report.pdf", type: "APPLICATION/PDF", ...}]

# `attachments`

```elixir
@spec attachments(Plover.Response.BodyStructure.t()) :: [map()]
```

List attachments in the message.

A part is considered an attachment if its disposition is `"ATTACHMENT"`
(case-insensitive), or if it has a filename in disposition or body params
and is not `"INLINE"`.

Returns a list of maps with keys: `:section`, `:filename`, `:type`, `:size`, `:encoding`.

# `charset`

```elixir
@spec charset(Plover.Response.BodyStructure.t()) :: String.t()
```

Get the charset from a body structure's params.

Looks for the `"CHARSET"` key (case-insensitive). Returns `"US-ASCII"`
as the default per RFC 2046.

# `encoding`

```elixir
@spec encoding(Plover.Response.BodyStructure.t()) :: String.t()
```

Get the content-transfer-encoding from a body structure.

Returns `"7BIT"` as the default per RFC 2045.

# `find_parts`

```elixir
@spec find_parts(Plover.Response.BodyStructure.t(), String.t()) :: [
  {String.t(), Plover.Response.BodyStructure.t()}
]
```

Find parts matching a MIME type pattern.

Supports exact matches (`"text/plain"`) and wildcard subtypes (`"text/*"`).
Matching is case-insensitive. Returns `{section_path, part}` tuples.

# `flatten`

```elixir
@spec flatten(Plover.Response.BodyStructure.t()) :: [
  {String.t(), Plover.Response.BodyStructure.t()}
]
```

Flatten a body structure tree into a list of `{section_path, part}` tuples.

Only returns leaf parts (not multipart containers). Section paths follow
RFC 9051 rules:

- Single-part message: `""`
- Multipart children: `"1"`, `"2"`, `"3"` (1-indexed)
- Nested multipart: `"1.1"`, `"1.2"` (dot-separated)

# `get_part`

```elixir
@spec get_part(Plover.Response.BodyStructure.t(), String.t()) ::
  {:ok, Plover.Response.BodyStructure.t()} | :error
```

Get a part by its section path (e.g., `"1.2"`).

Returns `{:ok, part}` or `:error` if the path is invalid.

---

*Consult [api-reference.md](api-reference.md) for complete listing*

[🔗](https://github.com/codonnell/plover/blob/main/lib/plover/command.ex#L1)

Represents an IMAP command to be sent to the server.

RFC 9051 Section 2.2.1 - Client Protocol Sender and Server Protocol Receiver

```elixir
@type t() :: %Plover.Command{args: list(), name: String.t(), tag: String.t()}
```

# Plover.Connection

Source: https://plover.hexdocs.pm/Plover.Connection.md

# `Plover.Connection`
[🔗](https://github.com/codonnell/plover/blob/main/lib/plover/connection.ex#L1)

GenServer managing a single IMAP connection.

Handles socket I/O, command dispatch, response accumulation,
and connection state machine transitions.

# `capabilities`

```elixir
@spec capabilities(GenServer.server()) :: [String.t()]
```

Returns the server's advertised capabilities as a list of strings.

# `child_spec`

Returns a specification to start this module under a supervisor.

See `Supervisor`.

# `mailbox_info`

```elixir
@spec mailbox_info(GenServer.server()) :: map() | nil
```

Returns mailbox metadata from the most recent SELECT or EXAMINE.

The returned map may include keys like `:exists`, `:flags`, `:uid_validity`,
and `:uid_next`. Returns `nil` if no mailbox is selected.

# `state`

```elixir
@spec state(GenServer.server()) ::
  :not_authenticated | :authenticated | :selected | :logout
```

Returns the current IMAP connection state.

Possible values: `:not_authenticated`, `:authenticated`, `:selected`, `:logout`.

---

*Consult [api-reference.md](api-reference.md) for complete listing*

# Plover.Content

Source: https://plover.hexdocs.pm/Plover.Content.md

# `Plover.Content`
[🔗](https://github.com/codonnell/plover/blob/main/lib/plover/content.ex#L1)

Content-Transfer-Encoding decoding and charset conversion for email body parts.

Decodes base64 and quoted-printable transfer encodings as specified in
RFC 2045, and converts common charsets to UTF-8 using only OTP stdlib.

## Examples

    # Decode base64 content
    {:ok, binary} = Plover.Content.decode(raw, "BASE64")

    # Decode quoted-printable with charset conversion
    {:ok, text} = Plover.Content.decode(raw, "QUOTED-PRINTABLE", "ISO-8859-1")

    # Decode and convert in one step
    {:ok, utf8_text} = Plover.Content.decode(raw, "BASE64", "Windows-1252")

# `convert_charset`

```elixir
@spec convert_charset(binary(), String.t()) :: binary()
```

Convert binary data from the given charset to UTF-8.

Supported charsets: UTF-8, US-ASCII, ISO-8859-1 (Latin-1), Windows-1252.
Unknown charsets return the data unchanged.

# `decode`

```elixir
@spec decode(binary(), String.t()) :: {:ok, binary()} | {:error, term()}
```

Decode content using the specified transfer encoding.

Supported encodings: `"BASE64"`, `"QUOTED-PRINTABLE"`, `"7BIT"`, `"8BIT"`, `"BINARY"`.
Encoding names are case-insensitive.

# `decode`

```elixir
@spec decode(binary(), String.t(), String.t()) :: {:ok, binary()} | {:error, term()}
```

Decode content using the specified transfer encoding, then convert
from the given charset to UTF-8.

# `decode_base64`

```elixir
@spec decode_base64(binary()) :: {:ok, binary()} | {:error, term()}
```

Decode base64 encoded data. Whitespace (line breaks) is ignored.

# `decode_encoded_words`

```elixir
@spec decode_encoded_words(String.t() | nil) :: String.t() | nil
```

Decode RFC 2047 encoded-words in a header value.

Encoded-words have the form `=?charset?encoding?text?=` where encoding is
`B` (base64) or `Q` (quoted-printable with `_` for space). Adjacent
encoded-words separated only by whitespace are concatenated per RFC 2047
Section 6.2.

Returns the decoded string. Passes through `nil` and plain strings
that contain no encoded-words.

# `decode_quoted_printable`

```elixir
@spec decode_quoted_printable(binary()) :: {:ok, binary()} | {:error, term()}
```

Decode quoted-printable encoded data per RFC 2045 Section 6.7.

- `=XX` hex pairs are decoded to the corresponding byte
- Soft line breaks (`=\r\n` or `=\n`) are removed
- All other characters pass through unchanged

---

*Consult [api-reference.md](api-reference.md) for complete listing*

---

# Plover.Protocol.CommandBuilder

Source: https://plover.hexdocs.pm/Plover.Protocol.CommandBuilder.md

# `Plover.Protocol.CommandBuilder`
[🔗](https://github.com/codonnell/plover/blob/main/lib/plover/protocol/command_builder.ex#L1)

Serializes `%Command{}` structs to iodata for transmission over the wire.

Handles IMAP astring quoting rules:
- Atom: if all chars are ATOM-CHAR, send as-is
- Quoted string: if contains spaces/parens/etc but no CR/LF, use quoted form
- Literal: for data with CR/LF or binary content

RFC 9051 Section 9 - Formal Syntax

# `build`

```elixir
@spec build(Plover.Command.t()) :: iodata() | {:literal, iodata(), binary()}
```

Build an IMAP command into iodata ready for transmission.

For most commands, returns iodata.
For APPEND (which requires a literal), returns `{:literal, first_part, literal_data}`
where `first_part` is iodata to send before the continuation, and `literal_data`
is the binary to send after receiving the continuation response.

# `build_done`

```elixir
@spec build_done() :: iodata()
```

Build the DONE command for ending IDLE.

---

*Consult [api-reference.md](api-reference.md) for complete listing*

---

# Plover.Protocol.Parser

Source: https://plover.hexdocs.pm/Plover.Protocol.Parser.md

# `Plover.Protocol.Parser`
[🔗](https://github.com/codonnell/plover/blob/main/lib/plover/protocol/parser.ex#L1)

Recursive-descent parser for IMAP response token lists.

Consumes token lists produced by `Plover.Protocol.Tokenizer` and
returns structured response data.

RFC 9051 Section 7 - Server Responses

# `token`

```elixir
@type token() ::
  {:atom, String.t()}
  | {:number, integer()}
  | {:quoted_string, String.t()}
  | {:literal, binary()}
  | {:flag, String.t()}
  | nil
  | :lparen
  | :rparen
  | :lbracket
  | :rbracket
  | :star
  | :plus
  | :crlf
```

# `tokens`

```elixir
@type tokens() :: [token()]
```

# `parse`

```elixir
@spec parse(tokens()) :: {:ok, term()} | {:error, term()}
```

Parse a token list into a response struct.

# Plover.Protocol.ResponseEncoder

Source: https://plover.hexdocs.pm/Plover.Protocol.ResponseEncoder.md

# `Plover.Protocol.ResponseEncoder`
[🔗](https://github.com/codonnell/plover/blob/main/lib/plover/protocol/response_encoder.ex#L1)

Serializes response structs to IMAP wire-format strings.

This is the inverse of `Plover.Protocol.Parser` — it takes the same struct
types that the parser produces and encodes them back to valid IMAP protocol
strings. Primarily useful for the `Plover.Transport.Mock` higher-level API,
which lets users build test responses from structs rather than raw wire protocol.

See the [Testing Guide](testing.md) for usage examples.

# `encode`

```elixir
@spec encode(struct()) :: binary()
```

Encode a response struct to an IMAP wire-format binary string.

# `encode_untagged`

```elixir
@spec encode_untagged(
  atom(),
  keyword()
) :: binary()
```

Encode an untagged status response (OK/NO/BAD/BYE).

# Plover.Protocol.Tokenizer

Source: https://plover.hexdocs.pm/Plover.Protocol.Tokenizer.md

# `Plover.Protocol.Tokenizer`
[🔗](https://github.com/codonnell/plover/blob/main/lib/plover/protocol/tokenizer.ex#L1)

Tokenizes IMAP response lines from binary data into a token stream.

Uses NimbleParsec for compile-time parser generation. The generated code
is pure binary pattern matching with no runtime dependency on NimbleParsec.

RFC 9051 Section 9 - Formal Syntax

# `parse_line`

```elixir
@spec parse_line(binary(), keyword()) ::
  {:ok, [term()], rest, context, line, byte_offset}
  | {:error, reason, rest, context, line, byte_offset}
when line: {pos_integer(), byte_offset},
     byte_offset: non_neg_integer(),
     rest: binary(),
     reason: String.t(),
     context: map()
```

Parses the given `binary` as parse_line.

Returns `{:ok, [token], rest, context, position, byte_offset}` or
`{:error, reason, rest, context, line, byte_offset}` where `position`
describes the location of the parse_line (start position) as `{line, offset_to_start_of_line}`.

To column where the error occurred can be inferred from `byte_offset - offset_to_start_of_line`.

## Options

  * `:byte_offset` - the byte offset for the whole binary, defaults to 0
  * `:line` - the line and the byte offset into that line, defaults to `{1, byte_offset}`
  * `:context` - the initial context value. It will be converted to a map

# `tokenize`

```elixir
@spec tokenize(binary()) :: {:ok, list(), binary()} | {:error, term()}
```

Tokenize one IMAP response line from binary data.

Returns `{:ok, tokens, rest}` on success, or `{:error, reason}` on failure.
Parses one complete response line (up to and including CRLF).
Any data after the CRLF is returned as `rest`.

---

*Consult [api-reference.md](api-reference.md) for complete listing*

---

# Plover.SequenceSet

Source: https://plover.hexdocs.pm/Plover.SequenceSet.md

# `Plover.SequenceSet`
[🔗](https://github.com/codonnell/plover/blob/main/lib/plover/sequence_set.ex#L1)

Parse and format IMAP sequence sets.

RFC 9051 Section 9 Formal Syntax:
  sequence-set    = (seq-number / seq-range) ["," sequence-set]
  seq-range       = seq-number ":" seq-number
  seq-number      = nz-number / "*"
  nz-number       = digit-nz *DIGIT

# `range`

```elixir
@type range() :: {Plover.Types.seq_number(), Plover.Types.seq_number()}
```

A single range in a sequence set, where both endpoints may be `:star`.

# `format`

```elixir
@spec format([range()]) :: String.t()
```

Formats a list of range tuples into an IMAP sequence set string.

## Examples

    iex> Plover.SequenceSet.format([{1, 5}, {10, :star}])
    "1:5,10:*"

    iex> Plover.SequenceSet.format([{3, 3}])
    "3"

# `parse`

```elixir
@spec parse(String.t()) :: {:ok, [range()]} | {:error, :invalid}
```

Parses an IMAP sequence set string into a list of range tuples.

Single numbers become `{n, n}` tuples. The wildcard `*` becomes `:star`.

## Examples

    iex> Plover.SequenceSet.parse("1:5")
    {:ok, [{1, 5}]}

    iex> Plover.SequenceSet.parse("1,3:5,10:*")
    {:ok, [{1, 1}, {3, 5}, {10, :star}]}

---

*Consult [api-reference.md](api-reference.md) for complete listing*

---

# Plover.Transport

Source: https://plover.hexdocs.pm/Plover.Transport.md

# `Plover.Transport`
[🔗](https://github.com/codonnell/plover/blob/main/lib/plover/transport.ex#L1)

Behaviour for IMAP transport connections.

Abstracts over SSL (production) and Mock (testing) transports.

# `option`

```elixir
@type option() :: {:active, :once | false}
```

# `socket`

```elixir
@type socket() :: any()
```

# `close`

```elixir
@callback close(socket()) :: :ok | {:error, term()}
```

Closes the connection.

# `connect`

```elixir
@callback connect(String.t(), :inet.port_number(), keyword()) ::
  {:ok, socket()} | {:error, term()}
```

Establishes a connection to the given host and port.

# `controlling_process`

```elixir
@callback controlling_process(socket(), pid()) :: :ok | {:error, term()}
```

Transfers socket ownership to another process.

# `send`

```elixir
@callback send(socket(), iodata()) :: :ok | {:error, term()}
```

Sends data over the connection.

# `setopts`

```elixir
@callback setopts(socket(), [option()]) :: :ok | {:error, term()}
```

Sets socket options (e.g., `active: :once`).

# `tag`

```elixir
@callback tag() :: atom()
```

Returns the message tag used for active-mode delivery.

SSL uses `:ssl`, Mock uses `:mock_ssl`.

# Plover.Transport.Mock

Source: https://plover.hexdocs.pm/Plover.Transport.Mock.md

# `Plover.Transport.Mock`
[🔗](https://github.com/codonnell/plover/blob/main/lib/plover/transport/mock.ex#L1)

Mock transport for testing. Each mock socket is a GenServer process
that stores enqueued responses and records sent data.

## Low-Level API

Use `enqueue/2` to enqueue raw IMAP wire-format strings:

    Mock.enqueue(socket, "* OK [CAPABILITY IMAP4rev2] Server ready\r\n")

## High-Level API

Use struct-based helpers that handle wire encoding and tag tracking
automatically:

    Mock.enqueue_greeting(socket, capabilities: ["IMAP4rev2"])
    Mock.enqueue_response(socket, :ok, text: "LOGIN completed")
    Mock.enqueue_response(socket, :ok,
      untagged: [%Mailbox.Exists{count: 10}],
      text: "SELECT completed"
    )

Tags are auto-generated (A0001, A0002, ...) matching the Connection's
tag counter. See the [Testing Guide](testing.md) for full examples.

# `child_spec`

Returns a specification to start this module under a supervisor.

See `Supervisor`.

# `enqueue`

Enqueue data that will be delivered to the controlling process
when active mode is set.

# `enqueue_continuation`

Enqueue a continuation response (`+`). Does not increment the tag counter.

## Options

  * `:text` - continuation text (default: `""`)

## Examples

    Mock.enqueue_continuation(socket, text: "Ready for literal data")
    Mock.enqueue_continuation(socket)

# `enqueue_greeting`

Enqueue a server greeting. Does not increment the tag counter.

## Options

  * `:capabilities` - list of capability strings (e.g., `["IMAP4rev2", "IDLE"]`)
  * `:text` - greeting text (default: `"Server ready"`)

## Examples

    Mock.enqueue_greeting(socket, capabilities: ["IMAP4rev2"])
    Mock.enqueue_greeting(socket, capabilities: ["IMAP4rev2", "IDLE"], text: "Ready")
    Mock.enqueue_greeting(socket, text: "Server ready")

# `enqueue_response`

Enqueue a tagged response with optional untagged responses preceding it.
Auto-generates the next tag (A0001, A0002, ...) atomically.

## Options

  * `:untagged` - list of response structs to encode before the tagged response
  * `:code` - response code (e.g., `%Capability{capabilities: ["IMAP4rev2"]}`)
  * `:text` - response text (default: `""`)

## Examples

    Mock.enqueue_response(socket, :ok, text: "LOGIN completed")

    Mock.enqueue_response(socket, :ok,
      untagged: [
        %Mailbox.Exists{count: 172},
        %Mailbox.Flags{flags: [:seen, :draft]}
      ],
      code: {:read_write, nil},
      text: "SELECT completed"
    )

    Mock.enqueue_response(socket, :no, text: "access denied")

# `get_sent`

Get all data that was sent through this mock socket.

---

*Consult [api-reference.md](api-reference.md) for complete listing*

---

# Plover.Types

Source: https://plover.hexdocs.pm/Plover.Types.md

# `Plover.Types`
[🔗](https://github.com/codonnell/plover/blob/main/lib/plover/types.ex#L1)

Shared type definitions for the Plover IMAP client.

# `conn`

```elixir
@type conn() :: GenServer.server()
```

A connection process identifier.

# `fetch_attr`

```elixir
@type fetch_attr() ::
  :envelope
  | :flags
  | :uid
  | :body_structure
  | :internal_date
  | :rfc822_size
  | {:body, String.t()}
  | {:body_peek, String.t()}
```

A FETCH data item to request.

Atoms request standard attributes. Tuple forms request body content:

  * `{:body, section}` - fetches the section and sets the `\Seen` flag
  * `{:body_peek, section}` - fetches the section without setting `\Seen`

# `flag`

```elixir
@type flag() :: atom()
```

A message flag atom (e.g., `:seen`, `:flagged`, `:deleted`).

# `mailbox_name`

```elixir
@type mailbox_name() :: String.t()
```

An IMAP mailbox name.

# `response_code`

```elixir
@type response_code() ::
  nil
  | Plover.Response.Capability.t()
  | {:permanent_flags, [flag()]}
  | {:uid_next, pos_integer()}
  | {:uid_validity, pos_integer()}
  | {:append_uid, {pos_integer(), pos_integer()}}
  | {:copy_uid, {pos_integer(), String.t(), String.t()}}
  | {atom(), nil | String.t()}
```

A response code from a server status response (RFC 9051 §7.1).

Data codes carry a typed value. No-data codes are `{name, nil}` tuples —
common names include `:alert`, `:parse`, `:read_only`, `:read_write`,
`:try_create`, `:closed`, `:authentication_failed`, `:expired`,
`:contact_admin`, `:no_perm`, `:in_use`, `:over_quota`, `:nonexistent`,
and others from RFC 9051 §7.1. Unrecognized codes from extensions are
`{atom(), nil | String.t()}`.

# `seq_number`

```elixir
@type seq_number() :: pos_integer() | :star
```

A sequence number: a positive integer or `:star` (representing `*`).

# `sequence_set`

```elixir
@type sequence_set() :: [{seq_number(), seq_number()}]
```

A parsed sequence set as a list of `{from, to}` range tuples.

# `status_attr`

```elixir
@type status_attr() :: :messages | :recent | :unseen | :uid_next | :uid_validity
```

A STATUS attribute to query on a mailbox.

# `store_action`

```elixir
@type store_action() :: :set | :add | :remove
```

How flags are applied in a STORE command.

# `store_silent`

```elixir
@type store_silent() :: boolean()
```

Whether the STORE command should suppress untagged FETCH responses.

# `untagged_response`

```elixir
@type untagged_response() ::
  Plover.Response.Capability.t()
  | Plover.Response.Condition.t()
  | Plover.Response.Enabled.t()
  | Plover.Response.Mailbox.Exists.t()
  | Plover.Response.Mailbox.Flags.t()
  | Plover.Response.Mailbox.List.t()
  | Plover.Response.Mailbox.Status.t()
  | Plover.Response.Message.Expunge.t()
  | Plover.Response.Message.Fetch.t()
  | Plover.Response.ESearch.t()
  | Plover.Response.Unhandled.t()
```

An untagged server response passed to the `:on_unsolicited_response` callback.
